newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed after a slow trading day, with a higher close in Tokyo aiding SMR grades sentiment, dealers said.

RSS rubber fell on further lack of participation from abroad, they said. "Buyers are still hoping to buy at lower levels as they know that the market can move downwards because of ample supplies," a dealer at a trading firm said.

Some enquiries of SMR rubber were seen from South Korea but dealers were unable to confirm any transactions. Some dealers said that Chinese buyers have turned their interest to THailand where prices are quoted slightly lower than Malaysia.
Trading was cautious as players adopted a cautious attitude at the start of the month following switch over to new trading months, dealers said.
At the close, November RSS 1 buyer fell 1.50 cents to 312.50 cents ($1.25) a kg but November SMR 20 buyer gained a cent at 308.50 cents.

The INRO five-day average was 243.31 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 30 from 244.27 on Sept 27. The daily indicator was 241.75 against 242.11. -- Tan Lee Lee (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5020 ringgit)
